subject: URGENT: Acme Prod degradation — reserved throughput under-delivery
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme-corp.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors and throughput drop (Acme)

Jordan —

We're seeing sustained elevated latency and 5xx errors across our production inference endpoints (all routed to your Dedicated pool for Acme). Over the last 3 hours the measured throughput that our service can push successfully has fallen to ~45% of the reserved capacity. We're getting frequent 429s and timeouts when traffic spikes, and this is directly affecting serving SLAs for customers.

Attached are a short sample of error traces and a CSV with minute-level throughput/latency numbers. Can someone on the Redwood side confirm whether we're being throttled, whether the Dedicated pool is saturated, or if there's a misrouting issue? This is hitting the product team and execs — need clarity + timeline for fix.

Symptoms:
- 429 and 503 errors on generation endpoints starting ~05:00 PDT
- p50 latency up from ~120ms to 350ms; p95 up to >1.2s
- Observed KV-cache misses on repeated prefixes

We need an ETA for mitigation and any temporary workarounds (re-routing to hosted variants, burst capacity, etc.).

—Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Platform Reliability Lead, Acme Corporation
(ops@acme-corp.com)

Subject: Re: Production errors and throughput drop (Acme)

Thanks Sarah — really sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as P1 and I've looped in SRE and our account team. Quick summary and next steps:

What we see so far (preliminary):
- Symptoms match Dedicated pool saturation / reduced effective throughput (observed by our telemetry).
- We're running a rolling check of GPU saturation and kernel-level stalls; preliminary traces show higher queue depth on several nodes.

Immediate mitigations we're initiating now:
1) Short-term capacity burst: request emergency +20% capacity on Acme's Dedicated pool (if available) to buy time for root-cause.
2) Canary re-route: prepare a fallback route to a compatible hosted model for non-sensitive requests (needs your sign-off).
3) Live SRE triage: Rishi will post findings and recommend config changes (batching / KV-cache policy adjustments).

I'll update you within 30 minutes with telemetry and an ETA for the burst. Neha / Marissa — please surface any contractual constraints (reserved throughput limits, overage billing) and whether we can pre-approve a temporary burst credit.

Jordan Blake

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Production errors and throughput drop (Acme) — initial triage

On Fri, Jul 3, 2026 at 8:56 AM jordan_blake@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Sarah — really sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as P1 and I've looped in SRE and our account team. Quick summary and next steps:

Sharing initial triage notes from SRE (high level):
- Root cause candidate: uneven allocation of request shards across the Dedicated GPU pool combined with increased long-sequence inference causing KV cache churn and GPU kernel stalls. This results in effective throughput well below committed throughput despite nominally available GPUs.
- Evidence: kernel-level queue depth spikes on nodes g-pool-07/08, higher device-side latency, and batch formation skew. See attached sample (we've uploaded additional traces to the incident ticket).

Immediate technical mitigations implemented (09:05 PDT):
- Rebalanced routing to spread shards across all nodes (reduces hot-spotting).
- Forced KV cache warmup on hot prefixes for 10 minutes to reduce misses.
- Temporarily disabled a new batching optimizer introduced last week which increased batch variance for long sequences.

Impact and ETA:
- These mitigations reduced 429 rates by ~60% within 10 minutes and p95 latency dropped from >1.2s to ~700ms. However throughput remains ~70% of committed for some customer slices.

Required next steps (needs exec decision / commercial sign-off):
- Approve emergency capacity burst (+20–30%) for up to 72 hours to restore headroom while we complete a permanent fix (kernel-level patch + routing change).
- If burst not approved, we propose downgrading routing for non-critical traffic to hosted model for up to 48 hours to preserve core SLA traffic.

I'll continue to post updates to the PagerDuty incident.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
